Notes on Rust lifetimes

June 11, 2024

A lifetime annotation never changes how long a value lives. It only describes how the lifetimes of several references relate to each other, so the compiler can check that no reference outlives the data it points to.

The classic example is a function returning the longer of two string slices. Without an annotation the compiler cannot tell which input the output borrows from.

fn longest<'a>(x: &'a str, y: &'a str) -> &'a str

Read more in my notes on borrowing.
